name: Pure
description: A streamlined GNOME desktop: one top panel, the overview for launching and switching, no permanent dock and an empty desktop. All standard GNOME keyboard shortcuts keep working.

settings.reason: JERONIX's primary look is dark; the light variant stays fully supported.
On Ubuntu, slate maps to the Yaru sage variant, the closest system accent to the JERONIX sage.
The overview is Pure's launcher and switcher, so it stays one gesture away.
The clock is the only persistent text in the panel; the weekday makes it useful at a glance.
Minimal title bars. Minimize and maximize remain available from the keyboard and by double-click.
Super opens the overview; Pure depends on it for keyboard-first navigation.
Workspaces appear and disappear as needed, so there is nothing to configure.
Secondary monitors stay put while workspaces switch, the GNOME default.
Drag-to-edge and Super+Left/Right tiling.
JERONIX light wallpaper.
JERONIX dark wallpaper.
Fill the screen without distortion.
Charcoal shows while the wallpaper loads.
Lock screen matches the desktop.
Ubuntu's dock stops reserving screen space and only appears on demand.
The dock appears when the pointer reaches the bottom edge.
The dock hides whenever a window would overlap it.
Bottom placement matches the overview's dash.
A compact dock instead of a full-width bar.
Fewer persistent items; Trash stays in Files.
Fewer persistent items; drives stay in Files.
An empty desktop.
An empty desktop.
An empty desktop.

recommended.reason: JERONIX panel, menu, overview and notification styling. Enable it yourself; layouts never enable or disable extensions.

limitations: Ubuntu's dock (ubuntu-dock) and desktop icons (ding) are configured, not disabled. Turning them off changes the enabled-extensions list, which Pure leaves to the user and to Layout Studio (Milestone 5).
Settings marked optional are skipped when their extension's schema is not installed (for example on non-Ubuntu GNOME).
Panel contents, overview structure and window behavior beyond these GSettings keys cannot be changed by configuration. That needs a JERONIX extension.
